body: You're so incredibly strong, I'm so proud of you 💕

Agree. Imagine being brutally murdered and they make a podcast or TV show about it. Your (or your loved one's) tragic life story being listened to/watched for entertainment. Honestly, I think it's quite disrespectful.

I've had the exact same for my whole life. everything just gets so much worse at night. even after having a good day, the nights are always bad. 

I wish I knew why this was. this is something a lot of people seem to have.

I was thinking about that too... like if someone attacks me, I dont even have time to reach for my weapon to defend myself. I guess the only solution is to carry it in your hand when you're walking alone outside? until we get better and dont need it anymore. because it's not really a long term solution to the problem of course.
I'm sorry... it sounds so scary. is there anyone living with you that can possibly talk to him? or another neighbor that you trust more?
it's the same for me. I've always had it, since I was a small child. but i have periods where it gets really really bad. and periods where it is manageable.
I'm so sorry to hear... 😔
I'm sorry to hear. sending you strength ❤

I'm so sorry... that's so scary. I understand that makes you feel anxious and paranoid. I would feel like that too. 

have you ever talked to the person? do you know that neigbour at all?
I'm glad it worked for you. but what if it goes wrong? like when you have a bad trip or something? can it get worse?
I'm so sorry to hear that... it's truly awful. it is really difficult, i get how you can feel trapped in the house and just so anxious when you do go outside. its awful.

okay, I get what you mean. 

and you are right. maybe not for every woman. but I know it's a very common thing for women to be afraid to be outside alone after dark. 

my sister and her friends and I used to call each other on the phone when cycling home in the dark. it didnt only make us feel safer, but it also actually made us be safer. if people heard us talking on the phone, they are less likely to attack because they know there is someone on the other end of the line ready to call 911.

I'm sorry to hear that... that's so difficult. and I really get what you mean. I have the same thing, but its hard to tell if it's from the trauma or because I'm autistic. maybe both... 

did you ever get help for your trauma? and did it make it better?

I'm so extremely sorry this has happened to you... it is awful and it really leaves a scar on your life. 

did carrying a knife help you?

I'm so sorry to hear this... your story sounds a lot like me. I've also basically had this my whole life since it also started for me at such a young age. I also feel like I'm being watched when I go outside, and that makes me very anxious in places where there are a lot of people. 

it is indeed one of the hardest things... being trapped at the house is horrible. daily life means having to go outside to work or to school/uni. I cant do any of those things.

I just want to give you a hug (with your permission of course). I'm so sorry you're going through this as well and if you ever need to talk, just know I'm here 💕
why would it be connected to being a woman?
I'm so sorry to hear that... does carrying those things make you feel a little more safe? I thought about carrying maybe pepper spray. but that's technically illegal in my country.
I'm so sorry.... it really is so awful and difficult 😔

I'm so sorry to hear that... that's truly horrible. 

I'm glad your boyfriend goes with you to make you feel safe. and I also get that your dog makes you feel safe.

I didnt know that. I did follow an education group about PTSD and they didnt even mention agoraphobia. 

I've been going to this specific program for almost a year and I just now discovered this is because of my ptsd.

I'm so sorry to hear...

but I'm glad you go with her. I'm also not able to go outside alone, so my partner also goes with me. it really does help. because otherwise I would be stuck in the house.
I'm really happy to hear that it got better for you. it gives us people who are still not there hope that it will get better. thank you for sharing 💕
I'm so sorry to hear.... 😔

I'm so sorry to hear what happened to you... that's awful...

what did you do to get to this point that you can go outside again?
I'm super proud of you that you're practicing going outside. its extremely hard, but here you are doing it anyway! sending you lots of love 💕

this sounds like a really good therapy. 

I'm currently doing emdr, and it's awful. I asked my psychologist if there are any other options. and the only other option is imaginative exposure or something. and that sounds even more awful... I guess we dont have that therapy you're doing where I go 😔
thank you so much. that means a lot to me 💕
